name: Italian Game
idea: Develop the bishop to c4, aim at f7, and bring the knights out before attacking.
mistakes: Pushing too many pawns before the pieces are developed, or moving the same piece twice without a reason.

line.note: White claims space in the centre.
The knight attacks e5 and prepares castling.
The Italian bishop looks toward f7.

name: Queen's Gambit
idea: Offer the c-pawn to draw Black's pawn off d5, then take the centre back.
mistakes: Treating the gambit as a sacrifice you must win back on the next move, or leaving the c8 bishop shut in.

line.note: The declined line keeps a pawn on d5 and opens a path for the dark bishop.
Black develops before deciding how to free the light bishop.

name: Sicilian Defence
idea: Black fights for the c-file and an asymmetrical pawn structure instead of copying White.
mistakes: Opening the position before the king is safe, or grabbing a pawn on c3 without checking the tactics.

line.note: White begins with the king's pawn.
Black fights for d4 from the flank.
Black controls e5 and opens the light bishop.
The knight recaptures and stands in the centre.
